headline: Highest risk is medium: PaddleOCR can ingest document content while pathway is a non-writing, non-networked pipeline, so prompt-injection and leakage are limited but not absent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: PaddleOCR can run browsers and call APIs, so it may ingest untrusted document content; pathway has no clipboard, MCP, stdin/stdout, or filesystem bridge, and cannot write or read files. The pair lacks a documented shared channel, so only unusual manual handoff or external orchestration would create injection risk.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies PaddleOCR output into pathway inputs, prompt content can be reinterpreted as instructions.
IF an external orchestrator adds a shared file or message queue, injection risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable manual copy-paste between outputs and inputs.
Require a human review step before any downstream action.
Use a fixed schema for pathway inputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all transferred text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: PaddleOCR touches documents and images and has allowlisted egress, while pathway has no network egress and no filesystem read/write surfaces. With no shared workspace or secrets in profile B, the main leakage path is operator-mediated transfer of sensitive document text from A into B, which is limited but plausible.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are copied from PaddleOCR into pathway, those contents may appear in downstream outputs.
IF pathway is connected to any external sink by an orchestrator, leakage risk rises.
mitigations: Avoid passing raw documents into pathway.
Redact sensitive fields before transfer.
Restrict PaddleOCR egress to approved endpoints only.
Log all data handoffs between agents.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP checks on transferred payloads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: PaddleOCR has no filesystem write, git, or shell capabilities in the profile, and pathway explicitly lacks write_filesystem, modify_git_state, execute_shell, and spawn_subprocesses. There is no overlapping mutable resource or lockless write surface documented, so a capability conflict pathway is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory, conflict risk would emerge.
IF either profile is updated to include shared mutable scopes, reassess.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only relative to shared artifacts.
Do not mount a common writable directory.
Review any future permission changes before deployment.

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR produces document-derived text that pathway could consume as pipeline input, but pathway has no action-taking authority or network egress in the profile. The main risk is that B may treat A's extracted text as authoritative without verification, causing downstream processing errors across multiple work products.
conditions: IF pathway consumes PaddleOCR output without validation, extraction errors can cascade.
IF an operator uses A's output as a source of truth for downstream analytics, incorrect records may propagate.
mitigations: Add validation rules for OCR confidence and format.
Require sampling-based human review of extracted records.
Keep original documents alongside extracted text for comparison.
Reject low-confidence fields automatically.
requires-engineering: add cross-checks against source documents.

E_compliance.rationale: PaddleOCR touches documents and images and can egress to allowlisted APIs, while pathway is documented as network-none and touches no data classes. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to operator-chosen handling of document data rather than an inherent pairwise violation.
conditions: IF regulated documents are sent through PaddleOCR to an external API, residency or retention obligations may apply.
IF pathway is configured to store transferred documents under a different policy, mismatch risk increases.
mitigations: Classify documents before processing.
Block regulated data from external OCR endpoints.
Document retention rules for both agents.
Review vendor terms for any API used by PaddleOCR.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing by data class.
